text:
maya: Heads-up — started a quant bakeoff for ceres-13b across AWQ and GPTQ on our CUDA20/Triton+TRT-LLM stack. Hitting surprising accuracy deltas and a couple of truncated outputs on the TRT path.

sam: baseline numbers?

maya: baseline hosted fp16 run: EM 78.4%, ppl 7.1. Local AWQ pipeline (our runtime, no TRT-LLM) -> EM 76.2% (−2.2), GPTQ 4-bit -> EM 77.9% (−0.5). But when I run AWQ through Triton+TRT-LLM the EM drops to 72.0% (−6.4) and some outputs are cut off mid-sentence.

zoe: can you paste an example of the truncated output?

maya: example (input + outputs):
```
# input
"Summarize the clients' ask and next steps for migration."

# awq (vllm path)
"We should schedule a migration window for database freeze, prepare a runbook, and notify the customer success team. Next steps: ..."
 
# awq (trt-llm path)
"We should schedule a migration window for database freeze, prepare a runbook, and notify the" <-- stops here
```

maya: Also seeing warnings in Triton logs: `TRT-LLM: kernel mismatch fallback -> run reference kernel` and repeated `KV cache shape mismatch` on warmup.

ravi: hmm. two things to check: 1) ABI/symbol mismatches between TRT-LLM plugin binary and system CUDA, 2) quantization meta (per-channel vs per-tensor) assumptions that our TRT kernels violate. Did you build the trt-llm plugin against CUDA20?

maya: plugin reports: `trt-llm v0.9.2 (built_with_cuda=11.8, triton_abi=2.18)`. We're running system CUDA 12.0/20.0 stack on the new images.

lukas: that mismatch could explain fallback to reference kernels (and the truncation if the fast kernel silently drops tokens). Also TensorRT FP8/int8 paths changed in CUDA20/TensorRT 9.x — plugin MUST be rebuilt.

ci-bot: quick repro command I ran: 
```
docker run --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -v /models/ceres13:/models redwood/rt-llm-bench:latest \
  bash -c 'tritonserver --model-repository=/models --strict-model-config=false'
```

maya: here's a small Triton log snippet when running AWQ through-trt:
```
[2026-11-05 14:12:03] TRT-LLM: loading plugin libtrtllm.so
[2026-11-05 14:12:03] WARN TRT-LLM: plugin was built against CUDA 11.8, running on CUDA 12.0 -> symbol lookup fallback
[2026-11-05 14:12:10] INFO TRT-LLM: registered kernel awq_fused_attention_fp8
[2026-11-05 14:12:10] ERROR TRT-LLM: KV cache shape mismatch: expected [1,32,1024], got [1,16,1024] -> using reference
[2026-11-05 14:12:12] WARN TRT-LLM: fast kernel produced output size smaller than expected -> trimming to reference size
```

sam: wow. fast kernel trimming output is bad. we should treat that as a correctness bug in the plugin and fail fast.

ravi: agreed. repro matrix to run: CUDA 11.8 (legacy images), CUDA 12/20 images, and for each Triton version (2.18, 2.19, 2.20) and trt-llm builds (built_with_cuda=11.8 vs 12.0). Also check building trt-llm with `-DUSE_LEGACY_KERNEL=ON` toggle.

maya: I'll queue the matrix. quick perf/eval snapshot I ran locally:
- fp16 hosted: EM 78.4% (ppl 7.1)
- AWQ (vLLM, CUDA20 native path): EM 76.2% (ppl 7.9)
- GPTQ (vLLM): EM 77.9% (ppl 7.3)
- AWQ (Triton+TRT-LLM, CUDA20, plugin built against 11.8): EM 72.0% (ppl 9.2) + 3 truncation cases / 300 eval samples

zoe: do we have a diff of logits or token probs for a failing example? that would show whether it's numeric drift vs structural runtime bug.

maya: dumped token probs; pre-softmax logits differ massively for tokens after the truncation point. Looks like kernel computed smaller sequence length and didn't advance the KV properly.

lukas: short-term mitigation: add a runtime guard that rejects trt-llm fast kernel if KV shapes don't match expected dims; rollback to reference kernel but fail the request (non-silent). Long-term: rebuild trt-llm against CUDA20 and update CI.

infra-bot: scheduled infra test job `quant-bakeoff/ceres13b/trt-rebuild` on h100-az2 with CUDA=12.0 image for 2026-11-06 03:00 UTC.

ci-bot: automation suggestion: add `TRITON_DISABLE_FAST_KERNELS=1` env toggle in the bakeoff harness so we can compare exact correctness with/without fast kernels. I'll open a PR to the bench harness now.

sam: also validate quant metadata produced by AWQ pipeline (scale/zero-point). Are we using per-channel scales in the TRTL kernel? mismatch there can produce big deltas.

maya: AWQ metadata: per-channel asymmetric, channel axis=0. TRT-LLM's awq loader currently assumes per-tensor for some older plugin builds — another mismatch.

ravi: ok then it's 2x mismatch: binary abi + metadata shape assumption. fix plan: (1) block fast kernels if metadata mismatch (fail loudly), (2) rebuild plugin w/ CUDA20 + correct AWQ loader, (3) run the full matrix and compare EM + token-delta traces.

maya: I'll file an infra ticket and a bug in the TRT-LLM repo with logs + small repro (input + model shard + eval 10-sample).

zoe: thanks — if you want I can help strip the repro to a minimal model + sample so it's easier to run in CI.

maya: please — that'd be great. I'll attach the dumps to the ticket.

sam: timeline?

maya: infra test job scheduled overnight. If rebuild + small kernel fix goes well we can have a patch in ~2 days. Otherwise fallback for Dedicated customers: force vLLM path for AWQ until TRT-LLM rebuild is validated.

lukas: I'll also add a short note to the rollout checklist: when upgrading system CUDA/TensorRT, rebuild native inference plugins and run the quant-bakeoff matrix.

maya: thanks all. filing the bug/infra ticket now and will post updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
